If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to adjust for sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.33) and price is trending upward, increase forecast by 1–2% in late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, reduce forecast by 1–2% in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >3% from true path, apply a 0.5–1.0% correction in mid-horizon to align with sentiment-weighted mean.
